newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal rebels kidnap Indian lawmaker, bodyguards.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels kidnap Indian lawmaker, bodyguards.

text.p: Suspected tribal guerrillas kidnapped a state lawmaker with two bodyguards in India's northeastern state of Tripura on Thursday, police said.

Senior superintendent of police Nepal Das told Reuters the rebels kidnapped Tripura Hills Peoples Party lawmaker Debrata Koloi and his bodyguards in a pre-dawn attack. "Suspected guerrillas equipped with sophisticated weapons stormed the house of Koloi at 4.00 a.m. and kidnapped them at gun-point," Das said.
He said the attack occurred at Dhumachara town, 155 km (95 miles) north of the state capital, Agartala.
State Home (Interior) Minister Samar Chaudhary expressed concern over the abductions and said state government and police officials had rushed to the spot to supervise search operations.
"We are still trying to ascertain the identity of the guerrilla group behind the abductions," Chaudhary said.
It was the second abduction of a public figure in Tripura in two years.

In January last year All Tripura Tiger Force guerrillas kidnapped Pranab Debbarma, a member of the state's ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist), with his bodyguards. They were released after 11 months in captivity.

Dozens of guerrilla groups have been fighting for decades for independent homelands in India's northeast, which borders Bangladesh, Burma, Bhutan and China. The region is home to nearly 200 ethnic groups.
The separatist groups, some tribal and others with Maoist ideologies, operate in the region's seven hilly states and accuse New Delhi of ignoring the area's economy.
